post.title: A 256 GB phone shows 238?
post.caption:
A 256 GB phone can show 238 GB 📱 and nothing is missing.

The box counts a gigabyte the way storage makers do: 1 GB = 1 billion bytes (Apple's support page says so for every iPhone, iPad and Mac). Some apps and systems count the other way: 1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes. Same chip, bigger gigabytes, so a smaller number: 128 → 119, 256 → 238, 512 → 477, 1 TB → 931.

The gap grows with size: about 69 GB on a 1 TB phone, more than a whole 64 GB phone. And the formatting and the system use some space too ("actual formatted capacity less").

Buying a phone? Take about 7% off the box number, then choose for what's left. Which size is yours? 👇 Send this to the friend who's about to buy one.
keywords: how much storage do i need

sources.note: Apple Support, How storage capacity is measured on Apple devices (published 21 May 2024, read 24 Nov 2026): 'Manufacturers of storage devices measure storage capacity using the decimal system (base 10)... 1 GB = 1 billion bytes and 1 TB = 1 trillion bytes; actual formatted capacity less.' 'Additional storage space is used by factors such as the device's operating system.' Binary: '1 GB = 1,073,741,824 bytes and 1 TB = 1,099,511,627,776 bytes. Some apps and operating systems, such as iOS 10 and earlier ... report storage capacity using the binary system.' Our numbers are that division: 128e9/1,073,741,824 = 119.2; 256e9 = 238.4; 512e9 = 476.8; 1e12 = 931.3; 1 TB gap 68.7 GB (6.9%).
